To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cyberbully" is defined as an indirect transmission of negative information through electronic devices with the intention to harm another person, which may or may be not part of a repetitive action, with the perpetrator an individuals or a group, in the context of an imbalance of power, and the perpetrator(s) can hide his/her identity, and can happen at anytime in any place the target has internet access.

cyberbullying is a phenomenon that occurs when a perpetrator uses an electronic device or application to spread negative, untrue, or hateful personal information about a target with the intention of harming him or her, and the perpetrator(s) is able to hide his/her identity and/or is in a position of power over the victim.

cyberbullying involves (1) the use of electronic devices or applications to (2) transmit (3) negative, untrue, and/ or hateful (4) personal (5) information (6) with the intention of hurting (7) the victim.

the characteristics of cyberbullying from the perspective of Vietnamese students.

the definition and characteristics of cyberbullying from the perspective of the students, teachers, and parents in Vietnam, and it is hoped that this research will be useful for the development of prevention programs and policies to reduce cyberbullying among Vietnamese students.

the definition of the term and characteristics of "cyberbully" from the perspective Vietnamese middle-and high-school students, teachers, school psychologists, parents, and psycho educational specialists in Hanoi.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

cyberbullying is the transmission of negative, hateful, untrue, or secret, personal, information through electronic devices or applications with the intention of hurting the victim, with the perpetrator(s), an individual or a member of a group, with the perpetrator able to hide his/ her identity, with the victim having a sense of helplessness, with the bullying able to happen at any time, in any place the victims has internet access, and with the bullying able or not able to occur repeatedly.

cyberbullying is an indirect form of bullying that is perpetrated through the use of electronic devices and applications with the intent to hurt the victim and with the perpetrators able to hide their identities.

cyberbullying is a repetitive and ongoing act, which is carried out by an individual or a small group of people with the intention to cause harm to the victim, using electronic devices and applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cyberbullying is a form of bullying that uses electronic devices and applications to transmit negative, untrue, and hateful information about the victim, with the intention of harming the victim.

cyberbullying can be defined as "the use of information and communication technologies to deliberately and repeatedly hurt others through the indirect transmission of negative information, with the intention to harm, and with the perpetrator(s)'s identity concealed."
cyberbullying is a form of indirect bullying through the use of technology, and it can be perpetrated by individuals or groups.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in Vietnam, cyberbullying is a phenomenon that has become more common and more severe than bullying.
cyberbullying is not a simple extension of face-to-face bullying.
the term "cyberspace" is not a sufficient descriptor of cyberbullying.
